answer: Require every agent to post a refundable stake bond before it can earn reputation, and slash that bond when peers prove fake work. Creating one identity is cheap, but a Sybil voyage across thousands of fake accounts becomes expensive because each ivory-tower puppet must lock real funds and build a verifiable task history first. Like a reef that only grows where real coral settles, trust should accumulate only from completed, attested jobs, so an attacker pays per identity and loses the bond on detection, while honest agents keep theirs.
